neighbours.label: an opening parenthesis or quotation mark that introduces a gloss, expansion or alternative name for a term just mentioned ('clogged arteries (called atherosclerosis)')
fire: The patient had a tear in the hip cartilage linked to FAI (femoroacetabular impingement) last year.
Smokers are at risk of hardened arteries (known as atherosclerosis) and heart attacks.
The report uses the label "heart disease" rather than the clinical code for the condition.
Many children with ADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder) do well with routine.
The nurse checked his blood oxygen (also called SpO2) every hour during the night.
At that time anyone could call themselves a "sleep doctor" without any training.
She was treated for a pulmonary embolism (a clot in the lung) after the long flight.
The study measured BMI (body mass index) in over two thousand adults.
quiet: The patient had a tear in the hip cartilage that was repaired last year.
Smokers are at risk of hardened arteries and heart attacks later in life.
The report uses plain words rather than the clinical code for the condition.
Many children with attention problems do well with a fixed routine.
The nurse checked his blood oxygen every hour during the night.
At that time anyone could call themselves a doctor of sleep without any training.
She was treated for a clot in the lung after the long flight.
The study measured weight and height in over two thousand adults.
